exposure: eclampsia characteristics (e.g., timing of onset, preceding symptoms, severity of hypertension)
eclampsia management (e.g., hydralazine, magnesium administration, delay from admission to delivery)
cohort: The study included 93 women diagnosed with eclampsia at Karamara Regional Hospital in Eastern Ethiopia over a one-year period, representing an incidence among 3500 deliveries.
finding: The incidence of eclampsia was very high at 2.7%, with corresponding high maternal (34.7%) and perinatal (11%) case fatality rates, particularly in young, nulliparous women often lacking antenatal care and presenting late.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was performed in 17% of eclampsia cases, and instrumental delivery in 18% of cases.
